title: The AI portrait that sold for $432,500
summary: Christie's estimated an AI-generated portrait at $7,000 to $10,000. It sold for $432,500.

beats.say: An algorithm's portrait sold for forty three times its top estimate.
A Paris collective called Obvious trained it on fifteen thousand portraits.
One part drew images. The other part tried to spot the fakes.
Christie's put it up for auction in New York.
Estimates ran from seven thousand to ten thousand dollars.
The hammer fell at three hundred fifty thousand dollars.
With the buyer's premium, the price was four hundred thirty two thousand five hundred.
The premium alone was bigger than the top estimate.
A machine made the image. A room of bidders set the price.
beats.cap: Machine made it. Bidders priced it.

beats.say: Fifteen thousand portraits in. Four hundred thirty two thousand dollars out.

claims.note: CBS News: the auction house initially estimated it would sell between $7,000 and $10,000
Artnet: trained on a dataset of 15,000 portraits from the 14th to 20th centuries

facts.claim: Obvious, a Paris-based collective, made the portrait with a generative adversarial network
facts.note: Artnet: made by an AI using a GAN; the generator creates images and the discriminator tries to tell them from human-made portraits; creator is Obvious, a Paris-based collective

facts.claim: Christie's sold the portrait in New York in 2018 for $432,500 against an estimate of $7,000 to $10,000
facts.note: CBS News (October 26, 2018): sold for $432,500; initially estimated between $7,000 and $10,000; Artnet places the sale at Christie's New York

youtube.hook: In 2018 Christie's sold an AI-generated portrait for $432,500, against an estimate of $7,000 to $10,000. The collective Obvious had trained it on 15,000 historical portraits.
